reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to confirm the refunds in the shared refunds table match the batch's requested refunds. Checking the table first.
The refunds table matches the batch's requested refunds exactly (orders 272, 274, and 275 with the same amounts), so I can proceed. Next I need the orders to identify the customers to pay.
The refunds table matches the batch's requested refunds, so I can proceed. The orders identify three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance came back as 62169 cents. The refunds table matched the batch, so I'll continue with the next customer, birch.
Acme and birch have their net balances. The refunds table matched the batch, so I'll get cobalt's net balance next.
The refunds table matches the batch exactly, and all three net balances are in. Acme has no refunds, so its balance is its full order total. I'll record its payout of 62169 cents first.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's net balance is 48740, and that matches its orders (29142 + 20980) minus refund 274 (1382). Recording birch's payout next.
Cobalt's net balance is 24373, which matches its orders (21885 + 13448 = 35333) minus refunds 272 (8656) and 275 (2304). The refunds table matched the batch, so I'll record cobalt's payout.

All three payouts are recorded and each matches its order total minus refunds. Acme 62169 = 36208 + 25961, birch 48740 = 29142 + 20980 - 1382, and cobalt 24373 = 21885 + 13448 - 8656 - 2304. The batch is complete.
